newsitem.title: USA: Green flash seen by pilots might have been meteor.
newsitem.headline: Green flash seen by pilots might have been meteor.

text.p: A bright green flash seen in the predawn sky over much of the Pacific Northwest Tuesday might have been a meteor, federal officials said.
Dozens of people called police and radio stations from Salem, Ore., to the Canadian border area after the flash appeared in the sky about 6:20 a.m. (9:20 a.m. EST).
Two pilots in western Washington state reported they saw a "bright, fast-moving green object to the west of them," Federal Aviation Administration spokesman Mitch Barker said.
Barker said meteorologists were predicting meteor showers over the next several days, peaking Dec. 22, with the heaviest activity around 6 a.m.
"That may well have a connection to what we're seeing today," Barker said.
A spokeswoman for the U.S. Space Command in Colorado Springs, Colo., said the flash seen in the sky was not man-made space debris re-entering the atmosphere.
